6	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Dragging to select a file name now toggles the row (confidence medium)**\n\nThe row's `onClick` fires for any click whose target isn't the input. That includes the click Chromium sends after a drag-select when mousedown and mouseup both land inside the `<li>`. Someone who drags over `.rowNow` or `.rowAfter` to copy a long file name will untick (or re-tick) that row as a side effect. The change does show on screen (dimmed row, strikethrough, a different summary count and button label), but it's easy to miss after a copy. One fix is to skip the toggle when `window.getSelection()?.toString()` is non-empty. Another is to add `user-select: none` to `.rowSelectable`, if copying names isn't something users need.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",

The test now selects text, clicks the row and checks the box keeps its state. Kept text selectable rather than `user-select: none`, because copying long file names is useful here."

findings.title: Double-clicking a name to select it still toggles the row once
findings.body: The guard reads the selection when the click fires. A drag-select is covered: the selection exists by the time mouseup sends the click. A double-click on a word in `.rowNow` or `.rowAfter`, the usual way to grab a name, sends two clicks. On the first one nothing is selected yet, because Chromium selects the word on the second mousedown. So the first click toggles the row and only the second is skipped, and the row ends up flipped after the copy. Triple-click behaves the same way. One way to close this is to skip the toggle when `event.detail > 1`, though that alone doesn't undo the first click's toggle. Another is to toggle on the first click and toggle back on `onDoubleClick`. Or you can accept this edge case, since the dimmed row shows the change.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed. Line 216 returns early when `window.getSelection()` has text, so a drag that selects a name no longer toggles the row. The new test pins this by mocking a selection and checking that the box keeps its state. Keeping the text selectable makes sense for copying names. I left a separate note on the double-click case.

input.summary: The push fixes the drag-select toggle: the row's click handler now skips the toggle when text is selected, and a test covers it. One edge case remains, as a consider: double-clicking a word still toggles the row once, because nothing is selected yet when the first click fires.
